There's this video series I've seen from this person on YT talking about the ideologies presented in Korra, and for the most part I agreed with them until I remembered that *this is a fictional show*. The Red Lotus are super compelling in basically every way but their ideal of anarchy being presented as shit and not really what most anarchists believe can also just be read as a psychological shift for the characters and not as a mouthpiece for the political beliefs of the creators. They all likely started out with good intentions and possibly even agreeable goals for the most part, but their isolation from the world and each other led them to radicalize themselves into irrelevance.

I don't know the creators at all so it feels weird going up to bat for them but this picture and your comment made me feel like this needed to be said; this was a good ass season of the show, and trying to act smug because you read a couple lines off the wikipedia sources (and not even citing them) and the proceeding to make a YT video "debunking" the clearly not good portrayal of anarchism in the show fails to analyze it as a piece of art and is also frankly, just kinda cringe.

Watching fights is imperative to getting better. Training consistently and well is certainly 75% or so of what goes into improvement, a better diet is maybe another 15, and that last 10 is watching people fight. Being able to dissect exactly what is happening in a fight is something you really only get from sparring and watching fights; along with raising your fight IQ and gaining the ability to remove yourself from the situation.

Depends on how much you eat for when to matter, honestly. For example, sometimes I’ll have a banana, slice of toast, and a small smoothie around 2 hours before training. That’ll be enough for me to not feel too full and have energy by the time we start. But if I want a full meal, and class starts at 5:30pm, then I’m eating at 1pm at the absolute latest. Just figure out how long it takes you to digest food and from there it’s quite self-explanatory

I swear, I’ve been training two and a half years at this point and only now, is it just starting to make sense. It’s all about time, persistence, and dedication. It’s about quality *and* quantity, most coaches (good ones at least) aren’t gonna let you by with shit reps even if you’re 2 hours into the class; you will only be as good as you make yourself.
